originality.rationale: The primary accessible full text of Huillet (2003) yields separate gap-count and vacancy laws but no unique finite-n covariance sign transition; Moriarty et al. (2007) address gap-count marginal approximations. Huffer (1988), known only from its abstract, already treats joint moments for the exact two variables under a more general arc-size model, so novelty is restricted to the nontrivial global sign classification and its sharp second-order root scaling, not the exact moment formula. Search yielded no matching published statement, but missing Huffer full text remains a material priority risk; this is a provisional self-review originality judgment, not uniqueness proof.

value.rationale: In fixed-size fragment coverage, number of gaps and total uncovered length measure different aspects of incomplete coverage. Their covariance surprisingly changes sign at a single sharp finite-size depth, which matters when relating fragmentation and total missing mass (e.g., circular genomic library coverage). Determining all finite-n signs and an explicit second-order nontrivial transition boundary is a motivated complete structural classification, not a small arbitrary numerical improvement. The result is confined to the natural equal-arc model.
